text:
Maya: quick thought — can we move the compatibility gate earlier in the intake flow? i.e., do a fast ABI/tokenizer compatibility pass before any bench runs. would save compute and reduce churn.
Liam: +1 on saving bench cycles. what's the minimal check set though? tokenizer map + opset fingerprint?
Sofia: minimal = tokenizer vocab mapping + kv-cache layout sanity + dtype/quantization shape checks. those fail fast and are cheap.
Maya: exactly. propose a tiny "entry-gate" that runs in <1s: tokenize sample inputs, verify token ids map, run a tiny forward on a micro-batch (1 seq) to validate shapes. if pass -> enqueue full smoke bench.
Liam: how do we represent the compatibility result? boolean? structured reasons? we want to index failures for flakiness analysis.
Sofia: structured. think of a small schema: reason_code, component, evidence (short). e.g. {code: "TOKENIZER_MMAP_MISMATCH", comp: "tokenizer", evidence: "id 345 != expected 345"} 
Maya: agreed. store in model metadata so downstream can query. also expose on console.
Alex: concern: fast forward requires a runtime kernel set. If the micro-forward runs on a host with different kernel selection than prod runtime might pick, we get false negatives.
Sofia: good point. we should run micro-forward in the same sandbox image the model will run in (same kernels). that's doable in Dedicated and Private, for hosted maybe use fingerprint-based emulation instead.
DevOpsBot: deploy: entry-gate v1 scheduled on intake-workers-2, image: ml-sandbox:v2026-03-01.
Liam: what about versioning the gate itself? if we change rules we want reproducible results across time. semver the gate + embed gate-version in the model record.
Maya: yep: gateway_semver field. also pin tokenizer spec version and opset mapping version.
Sofia: tradeoffs: moving checks left increases latency on "fast" onboarding path, but saves wasted bench resources. We need configurable policy: team-level (fast path) vs strict (enterprise) profiles.
Alex: another edge: quantized binaries — their kernels may differ subtly across hardware (e.g., q8->q4 degradation). entry-gate should allow a "compatibility tolerance" flag: fail-only-if-major.
Maya: propose default tolerance=medium, enterprise=zero-tolerance. store as string in intake.yaml.
Liam: implementation sketch: 1) tokenizer-only check (stateless) 2) micro-forward with deterministic seed + small golden tensor compare (L2 norm threshold) 3) if either fails => short-circuit.
Sofia: sample golden compare snippet (pseudo):
```
# micro-forward golden compare
seed = 42
x = randint(seed, shape=(1,16))
out = model.forward(x)
if l2(out, golden) > THRESHOLD: fail(reason="GOLDEN_MISMATCH")
```
Alex: where do we keep golden tensors? central immutable store keyed by model family + gate-version. must be small.
Maya: ops: agree. small n-dim tensors in blobstore + content-hash. golden updates only via gated process.
Liam: alerting: if entry-gate fails repeatedly for 3 models in a day, page infra team. add a metric: entry_gate_fail_rate.
DevOpsBot: metric created: metric.entry_gate_fail_rate (1m, 5m).
Sofia: API surface: intake API returns early verdict: {status: "queued", entry_gate: {state: "pass"|"fail", reasons: [..], gate_version: "1.0.0"}}. keep payload small.
Maya: UX: in console show a quick "fast-check" badge with link to evidence; allow re-run entry-gate after small fixes.
Alex: rollout plan: alpha on internal models (1 week), then opt-in beta for hosted customers, then default for new intake.
Liam: docs: short doc + example of failing tokenizers + remediation steps. I'll draft.
Maya: action items:
- Liam: draft docs + schema for structured failures (due EOD Wed)
- Sofia: prototype micro-forward runner + golden compare (PR by Fri)
- Alex: define tolerance levels and failure semantics for quantized binaries (blocker?) (sync Thu)
- Ops: set up metric and gate-versioning (DevOpsBot already created metric)
Maya: thanks all. tagging @Liam @Sofia for followups. :thumbsup:
Liam: noted, will post design PR link when ready.
Sofia: will test on amd64 + nvidia images and share results.
Alex: adding small caveat: ensure entry-gate logs do not contain model weights or secrets. just hashes/evidence.
Maya: good call. redact accordingly.
DevOpsBot: reminder: intake-workers-2 has maintenance window tomorrow 02:00-03:00 UTC.
Maya: ok, we'll avoid scheduling big canary runs during that window.
